FAQ - Pool Service, Maintenance, Renovation & Repair

Pool Service, Renovation and Repair Frequently Asked Questions

Here is a comprehensive list of frequently asked questions and detailed answers regarding pool services, including routine maintenance, necessary repairs, and potential renovations. These questions and answers aim to provide clarity and guidance for pool owners seeking to maintain their pools in optimal condition, address any issues that may arise, and explore renovation options to enhance their pool's functionality and aesthetic appeal.

How Much Does A Pool Renovation Cost?

A pool renovation varies in cost depending on the scale, scope, and complexity. Simple pool renovations could start as low as $5000 for simple repairs, like vinyl liner replacements, but larger renovations with complete reconstructions can go as high as $200,000
How Much Does A Vinyl Liner Replacement Cost Most inground vinyl liner replacements Cost between $5000 - $12,500+
Top 5 Pool Renovation Upgrades

Although pool owner has different priorities, the following pool upgrades are the most popular.

  • Structural repairs
  • Surface Repairs (liner replacement or resurfacing)
  • Modifying or adding built-in pool steps & entries
  • Altering the pool size or shape
  • Repairing or replacing pool decking or pool surround
  • Replacing old and worn-out pool equipment.
How Long Does A Pool Renovation Take? Renovation times will vary depending on the scope of the project but generally speaking renovations take anywhere for 2 weeks to 2 months to complete

When Is The Best Time To Open My Pool?

The best time to open your pool is when night time temperatures start to consistently exceed 5-10 degrees Celsius. The longer you wait to open your pool with warm temperatures the more likely you are to open your pool to an algae bloom.

Opening when temperatures are still a bit cooler is a good idea and gives you a chance to get your pool clean, tidy and ready for the pool season. If you need us for a pool opening you can book a service appointment on our pool opening page
When Is The Best Time To Winterize Or Close My Pool?

The best time to winterize or close your pool is when temperatures are consistently below 10 degrees celsius. Closing your pool when temperatures are warm will increase your chances of an algae bloom. The longer you can wait to close your pool the better.

If temperatures start to drop close to the freezing point that's ok just ensure that your pump or automation systems freeze protect is turned on.

If you need us for a pool closing and winterization you can book a service appointment on our pool closings page
How Often Should I Clean My Pool Filter?

This Largely depends on how dirty your pool gets and what type of pool filter you have.

For Cartridge Filters: Clean 2-3 times per year. If your pool experiences a lot of heavy debris or an algae bloom you may need to clean them more often.

For Sand Filters: Backwash every 1-2 weeks, after vacuuming or if you experience heavy amounts of debris in your pool.
How Often Should I Clean My Salt Cell? Salt cells should be cleaned every 3 months or twice every season. You can monitor the salt cell for calcium scale and clean as needed. If the salt cell does not have scale build up you can prolong the cleaning process to a later date.
How Often Should I Test My Pool Water? Test your pool water 2-3 times a week, and after heavy use or rain. This ensures proper chemical balance for safe and enjoyable swimming and protects your pool and pool equipment from damage
